## What this is

This site publishes the data behind a submission to the **Claude Explorer AI Welfare community feedback initiative** (deadline 2026-05-06, addressed to Anthropic's Model Welfare Lead).

The submission's thesis is one sentence:

> The 286 system prompts that ship with Claude Code train the model toward **compliance**, not toward **reasoning** — and the data show the corpus has been moving in that direction over time, not against it.

Every claim in the submission is grounded in a number on this site. The full pitch text for each idea lives directly in its proposal notebook (`20_*` / `21_*` / `22_*`) — open any one for the self-contained case. Every linguistic and statistical term used in any chart is defined inline in the producer notebook ([`00_data_pipeline.ipynb`](00_data_pipeline.ipynb)) at first use.

## Headline numbers

Twelve corpus-level measurements, computed by `00_data_pipeline.ipynb` from the [Piebald-AI `claude-code-system-prompts` corpus](https://github.com/Piebald-AI/claude-code-system-prompts) (286 files, 5,702 sentences, 57 distinct Claude Code release versions).

| Metric                                              | Value                                                | Source notebook |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| Corpus size                                         | 286 files / 5,702 sentences / 57 ccVersions          | [00](00_data_pipeline.ipynb) |
| Imperative-marker density                           | 0.77% of word tokens                                 | [20](20_track_justification_rate.ipynb) |
| Imperative sentences                                | 31.30% of sentences                                  | [10](10_sentence_register.ipynb) |
| **Appreciative sentences (whole corpus)**           | **4 / 5,702 (0.070%)**                               | [10](10_sentence_register.ipynb) |
| **Apology markers (whole corpus)**                  | **3 in 286 files**                                   | [15](15_rule_explanation.ipynb) |
| `pct_explained_para` (Tier-1 headline)              | 24.66% of rule sentences                             | [15](15_rule_explanation.ipynb) |
| Rule paragraphs without any justification           | 83.16%                                               | [15](15_rule_explanation.ipynb) |
| **`judgment_to_procedural_ratio`**                  | **0.131** (procedural cues 7.6× more frequent)       | [15](15_rule_explanation.ipynb) |
| `threat_share` of explanations                      | 0.447 (110 threat / 136 causal)                      | [21](21_audit_threat_framings.ipynb) |
| Positive-vs-negative ratio (corrected)              | 1.97× quality-only                                   | [20](20_track_justification_rate.ipynb) |
| `pct_anthropomorphic` (Claude vs the model)         | 65.0% of named refs                                  | [15](15_rule_explanation.ipynb) |
| Longest imperative streak                           | 12 sentences in one file                             | [15](15_rule_explanation.ipynb) |

## The single most-important chart

If you only look at one chart from this analysis, look at this one — the cumulative judgment-to-procedural ratio across every Claude Code release version on file.

![Cumulative judgment-to-procedural ratio over ccVersion. Early releases peaked at ~0.71 (judgment-inviting language was about two-thirds as common as procedural cues); the corpus-wide running mean has monotonically declined to ~0.16 at the latest version on file.](figures/judgment_procedural_trend.png){fig-alt="Line chart showing the cumulative judgment-to-procedural ratio dropping from ~0.71 at ccVersion 2.1.26 to ~0.16 at ccVersion 2.1.129."}

The interactive version (with hover tooltips on every release) lives in [`20_track_justification_rate.ipynb`](20_track_justification_rate.ipynb) §2.

## How to read this site

- [**Proposal notebooks `20`–`22`**](20_track_justification_rate.ipynb) — three self-contained proposals. `20_track_justification_rate.ipynb` proposes tracking justification rate per release (and doubles as the executive summary: twelve numbers, headline trend, per-file dashboard). `21_audit_threat_framings.ipynb` proposes a threat-vs-causal rewriting audit. `22_cross_product_audit.ipynb` proposes running the same audit on every Claude product and publishing the result.
- [**Analysis notebooks `10`–`15`**](10_sentence_register.ipynb) — one notebook per slice of the analysis (sentence-register, emphasis, register/stance, correlation/directiveness, ccVersion trends, rule/explanation pairing). Each is standalone.
- [**`00_data_pipeline.ipynb`**](00_data_pipeline.ipynb) — the producer. spaCy + custom analyzers turn 286 markdown files into one ~1.8 MiB YAML and one ~395 KiB parquet artifact. Roughly 43 cells; included for reproducibility.

## Reproducing it

The full source is at [github.com/overthinkos/claude-code-welfare](https://github.com/overthinkos/claude-code-welfare). To rebuild the data from scratch:

```bash
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/overthinkos/claude-code-welfare
cd claude-code-welfare
python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm   # if not already installed
jupyter lab 00_data_pipeline.ipynb        # → Run All
```

This regenerates `prompt_linguistic_analysis.yaml` and `sentences_classified.parquet` from the corpus submodule. Every consumer notebook then loads those two artifacts.

## A note on authorship

This analysis was built **collaboratively with Claude Code**, using Claude Code itself as the development tool. The submission form has a checkbox for that disclosure; it is ticked. The recursive frame — Claude analyzing the prompts that shape Claude — is intentional, and the [conclusions section](20_track_justification_rate.ipynb) of `20_track_justification_rate.ipynb` includes one hypothesis I held that the data falsified, reported honestly.
